questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a scalable, automated policy gate across multi-cloud clusters using Gatekeeper/OPA, Cosign attestations, and runtime security constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Cosign attestation and image provenance
- Registry allowlist and image provenance checks
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop capabilities
- CI integration and gatekeeper audit verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (Gatekeeper) minimal sketch
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecuredcontainers
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecuredContainers
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8ssecuredcontainers
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not signed(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Container image %v must be cosign-signed", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not allowed_registry(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Registry %v not in allowlist", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
          msg := "Container must run as non-root"
        }
```

## What to Look For

- Demonstrates understanding of OPA/Gatekeeper policy structure
- Shows proper cosign attestation validation approach
- Includes comprehensive runtime security constraints
- Outlines practical CI/CD integration strategy

## Why This Is Asked
Security of supply chain in multi-tenant, multi-cloud clusters is critical; signing and pinning mitigates tampering.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing (Cosign, Sigstore)
- Digest pinning (@sha256:...)
- Admission policies (Gatekeeper, Kyverno)
- CI verification with cosign verify

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-digest-signature
spec:
  rules:
  - name: digest-pinned
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ['Deployment','StatefulSet','DaemonSet','Job','CronJob']
    validate:
      message: 'Image must be pinned to a digest and Cosign-signed'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            metadata:
              annotations:
                cosignSig: 'true'
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@sha256:*'
```

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow sketch
name: Sign and Verify Image
on: [push]
jobs:
  sign-verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          docker build -t registry.example.com/project/model:tag .
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/project/model:tag
      - name: Verify image
        run: cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/project/model:tag
```

## Why This Is Asked
Assess practical use of OPA in Kubernetes, translating security expectations into verifiable policies; tests demonstrate understanding of Pod spec structure.

## Key Concepts
- Rego fundamentals
- PodSpec fields: volumes.hostPath, securityContext.privileged, capabilities
- OPA test framework and unit tests
- Admission testing approaches

## Code Example
```javascript
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  some vol in input.request.object.spec.volumes
  vol.hostPath
  msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  some c in input.request.object.spec.containers
  c.securityContext.privileged == true
  msg := "privileged containers are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  some c in input.request.object.spec.containers
  some cap in c.securityContext.capabilities.add
  cap == "NET_ADMIN"
  msg := "NET_ADMIN capability is forbidden"
}
```

## Compliant Pod Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: false
      capabilities:
        add: []
  volumes:
  - name: config
    emptyDir: {}
```

## Noncompliant Pod Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
      capabilities:
        add: ["NET_ADMIN"]
  volumes:
  - name: host-root
    hostPath:
      path: /
```

## Validation Plan
1. Test policy with OPA: `opa test -v policy.rego`
2. Validate compliant pod: `kubectl apply -f compliant.yaml`
3. Verify noncompliant rejection: `kubectl apply -f noncompliant.yaml --dry-run=server`

## Why This Is Asked

- Volume types (hostPath) and their risks

## Code Example

```yaml
name: k8s-security-gate
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          kubectl version --client
          kubeval manifests/*.yaml
          bash scripts/validate.sh
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
violations=0
for f in manifests/*.yaml; do
  if grep -qE "hostPath|runAsNonRoot|NetworkPolicy" "$f"; then :; else echo "General policy missing in $f"; violations=$((violations+1)); fi
  # pseudo-checks for brevity; real checks parse YAML (e.g., yq)
done
if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

## How It Works

Edge layers cache per-tenant state and call a central Redis-backed ledger via a Lua script that atomically consumes tokens. A regional coordinator ensures global quotas while keeping latency low. Time windows and heartbeat-based refresh bound drift. In Redis outage, fall back to in-process counters with strict backpressure and reconcile on recovery.

## Key Points

- **Atomicity**: Lua script executes in Redis to decrement tokens atomically.
- **Consistency**: cross-region quotas converge via central ledger with short TTL-based caches.
- **Failure handling**: circuit breaker, degraded mode with local counters, paced release when Redis returns.

## Example

```javascript
// Minimal working example
async function checkQuota(tenantId, tokens=1){
  const key = `quota:${tenantId}`;
  const now = Date.now();
  const lua = `
    local k = KEYS[1]
    local t = tonumber(ARGV[1])
    local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
    local cap = tonumber(ARGV[3])
    local need = tonumber(ARGV[4])
    local data = redis.call('hmget', k, 'tokens','last')
    local lol = tonumber(data[1] or cap)
    local last = tonumber(data[2] or now)
    local elapsed = math.max(0, now - last)
    lol = math.min(cap, lol + elapsed * rate / 1000)
    if lol >= need then
      lol = lol - need
      redis.call('hmset', k, 'tokens', lol, 'last', now)
      return lol
    else
      return -1
    end
  `
  const res = await redis.eval(lua, 1, key, now, rate, cap, tokens)
  return res
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CI policy enforcement skills using image signing—a common real-world requirement in production Kubernetes environments. It assesses understanding of supply chain security and GitOps practices.

## Key Concepts
- Container image signing with cosign
- Public key infrastructure for signature verification
- Manifest scanning in CI pipelines
- Handling signed vs. unsigned images in deployment gates
- GitOps workflow security

## Code Example

**GitHub Actions Workflow:**
```yaml
name: Verify Image Signatures
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'manifests/**'

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Extract image references
        id: images
        run: |
          echo "images=$(grep -roh 'registry.example.com/[^"]+' manifests/ | sort -u | jq -R -s -c '. | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          for image in $(echo '${{ steps.images.outputs.images }}' | jq -r '.[]'); do
            cosign verify --key cosign.pub $image
          done
```

**Sample Manifest (signed image):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0
```

**Failing Manifest (unsigned):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:unsigned
```

# Generate key pair
cosign generate-key-pair

# Sign an image

# Verify locally
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0

## Code Example
```yaml
# Failing manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  password: "s3cret123"
```
```yaml
# Passing manifest (ExternalSecret)
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: db-credentials
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    name: secrets-store
  data:
  - secretKey: password
    remoteRef:
      key: prod/db/password
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Understanding admission control and policy as code.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate, Constraint
- Rego-based policy, allowlist, image digest
- Pod spec image references and admission outcomes

## Code Example
```rego
package k8simagedigest
violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
  image := container.image
  digest := index_of(image, "@sha256:")
  not digest
  msg := "image must include a sha256 digest"
}
violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
  reg := strings.Split(image, "/")[0]
  allowed := input.parameters.allowed_registries
  reg notin allowed
  msg := "registry not allowlisted"
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simagedigest
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageDigestConstraint
  targets:
  - target: OPA
    rego: |
      package k8simagedigest
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        image := container.image
        digest := index_of(image, "@sha256:")
        not digest
        msg := "image must include a sha256 digest"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        image := container.image
        reg := strings.Split(image, "/")[0]
        allowed := input.parameters.allowed_registries
        reg notin allowed
        msg := "registry not allowlisted"
      }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageDigestConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-image-digest-allowlist
spec:
  allowed_registries: ["registry.company.local", "registry.dev.local"]
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.local/app@sha256:abcdef...
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.unauthorized.local/app:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test additional image attributes (size, architecture) in Gatekeeper? 
- How would you roll back a failing policy without downtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of resource isolation and guardrails in multi-tenant clusters, plus practical policy tooling.

## Key Concepts

- ResourceQuota
- LimitRange
- Pod resource requests/limits
- Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-resource-requests-limits
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod","Deployment","StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must define cpu/memory requests and limits"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  requests:
                    cpu: "+"
                    memory: "+"
                  limits:
                    cpu: "+"
                    memory: "+"
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle existing workloads that miss resources without disruption?
- What are trade-offs of using a namespace-level limit range vs per-deployment constraints?
